title: Consensus-weighted profile generator with reproducible seedbank and runner orchestration
creator: Zoe Chen
description:
Background:
We frequently see variance between eval runners and dataset sampling across profile generation runs. Small non-determinisms (tokenizer differences, sampling RNG, transient model state) cause published profiles to flip-flop and create noisy recommendations for model pinning and quantization. That increases churn during onboarding and makes guardrails for rollouts noisy.

Goal:
Create a benchmark harness extension that produces reproducible, consensus-weighted performance profiles suitable for publishing as the canonical profile artifact for a model version. Key parts: (1) a reproducible seedbank and deterministic orchestration layer so all runners sample the same prompts/deterministic RNG state; (2) a runner contract shim so each eval runner records provenance and flags non-deterministic operations; (3) an aggregator that computes consensus weights across runs and surfaces outliers; (4) profile artifacts that are diff-friendly and include provenance metadata to enable safe version pinning.

High-level approach:
- Seedbank service: lightweight, file-backed service (initially local to the harness) that produces named seed sequences per workload and exposes a stable seed manifest (sha256) that can be checked into artifact storage. Seed manifests will include seed id, per-run RNG seeds, prompt-sampling choices, and tokenizer checksum.
- Runner orchestration: extend the harness orchestration layer to accept a seed manifest id and broadcast per-run seeds to each runner. Each runner must honor RNG seeds for sampling operations and must surface a determinism report (flags for any op that required nondeterministic fallback).
- Consensus weighting aggregator: run each workload across N runners and M seeds (configurable, default N=3 runners x M=5 seeds). Compute per-example medians, interquartile ranges, and an agreement score. Use agreement score to downweight outlier runs when producing final profile numbers; include per-metric confidence intervals.
- Profile schema: produce a JSONL artifact with one row per workload+metric that includes: metric_name, aggregated_value, ci_lower, ci_upper, agreement_score, seed_manifest_sha, runner_ids, raw_run_values (indexed), tokenizer_checksums, and links to PRs/config used. Artifacts must be stable and diffable (sorted keys, consistent float formatting).

Acceptance criteria:
- Harness can generate a seed manifest and run the full pipeline end-to-end locally and in CI.
- Runners produce matching deterministic outputs for at least 95% of sampled prompts when using the seed manifest and configured RNG seeds on a stable model binary.
- Aggregator computes agreement_score and final aggregated metrics and stores a profile artifact in the artifact bucket with manifest SHA in filename.
- The profile artifact includes provenance (Git SHAs, harness config, tokenizer checksum, seed manifest id) and a diffable layout.
- New profile artifacts are consumed by the model-onboarding flow to produce a recommended pin and publication note.

Design notes & trade-offs:
- Determinism vs realism: forcing full determinism (e.g., deterministic tokenization and sampling with fixed RNG) may hide production variability. To balance, we record both deterministic-run outputs and an optional "no-seed" run to estimate field variance. Consensus weighting uses both types to give a conservative estimate.
- Seed source: initial plan uses a deterministic PRNG seed derived from a seed manifest; we evaluated using a KMS-backed RNG for cryptographic guarantees but it adds complexity. We chose deterministic PRNG with checksumed manifests for reproducibility across offline runs.
- Runner changes: we add a shallow contract (seed param + determinism report) to avoid invasive refactors. Runners that cannot honor deterministic sampling will still run but will be flagged and downweighted automatically.

Migration & rollout plan:
1) Implement seedbank and harness client shim (week 1-2).
2) Add runner shim and run 3 internal runners across a subset of onboarding workloads in canary mode (week 3).
3) Iterate on aggregator heuristics and CI integration; publish first consensus-weighted profiles for a small set of model versions (week 4).
4) Expand to broader runner fleet and add monitoring dashboards for agreement_score and seed manifest drift (week 5-6).

Monitoring & dashboards:
- New dashboard panels: agreement_score per workload, seed manifest drift (tokenizer checksum mismatches), percent of runs flagged nondeterministic, artifact publish latency.

Risks:
- Some runners (third-party or legacy) will not support deterministic sampling; we must ensure harness can still incorporate them without corrupting artifacts.
- Tokenizer drift across runner environments can make seeds ineffective; include tokenizer checksum check as a gate.

Next steps & open questions:
- Decide default N x M for consensus (proposal: 3x5).
- Finalize profile artifact filename convention and retention policy.
- Confirm whether seed manifests should be signed or just SHA-verified.
